options: The probability of A and B happening together
The probability of B given A
The probability of A among only the cases where B happened
The probability that A and B are independent
questions.explain: Conditional probability restricts attention to cases where B happened: P(A | B) = P(A and B) / P(B).

questions.q: In the table, 150 of 500 free-plan customers churned. What is P(churn | Free)?
questions.explain: 150 / 500 = 0.3. (0.15 is P(Free and churn) over all 1,000 customers; 0.75 is P(Free | churn).)

questions.q: Which condition defines independent events A and B?
options: A and B can never happen together
P(A | B) = P(A), so P(A and B) = P(A) x P(B)
questions.explain: Independence means knowing B does not change the probability of A.

questions.q: Two cards are drawn without replacement from a 52-card deck. Why is P(both aces) 4/52 x 3/51 rather than (4/52) squared?
options: Because the second card's probability depends on the first (an ace is gone), so the events are not independent
Because probabilities must add up to one
questions.explain: Drawing without replacement changes the deck, so the second factor is a conditional probability.

questions.q: Two events that are mutually exclusive, each with positive probability, are:
options: Dependent, because if one occurs the other is impossible
questions.explain: Knowing one happened tells you the other did not, so they are dependent.
